subject: Accountancy
central_question: How does a company classify its share capital and record the issue, allotment, forfeiture and reissue of equity and preference shares?
in_scope_units: Meaning and features of a company and the kinds of companies introduced in the chapter.
Meaning and categories of share capital: authorised, issued, subscribed, called-up, paid-up, uncalled and reserve capital.
Nature and classes of shares, including preference and equity shares and their rights.
Issue of shares through application, allotment and calls and the basic journal-entry sequence.
Calls in arrears and calls in advance, including interest and balance-sheet presentation.
Over-subscription, rejection, full allotment and pro-rata allotment; under-subscription and minimum subscription.
Issue at par, at premium, restrictions on issue at discount and issue for consideration other than cash.
Forfeiture of shares for non-payment, treatment of share capital and securities premium and reissue of forfeited shares.
Transfer of gain on reissue to Capital Reserve.
banned_topics: Issue and redemption of debentures, which belongs to the next chapter.
Buy-back, bonus issue and detailed redemption of preference shares beyond the chapter’s share-issue scope.

known_pitfalls.claim: Paid-up capital can exceed called-up capital.
known_pitfalls.correction: Paid-up capital is called-up capital less calls in arrears and therefore cannot exceed the amount called.

known_pitfalls.claim: Over-subscription increases subscribed capital beyond issued capital in the books.
known_pitfalls.correction: The company can allot only the offered number; excess applications are rejected, refunded or adjusted, so subscribed capital does not exceed issued capital.

known_pitfalls.claim: Securities premium is part of nominal share capital.
known_pitfalls.correction: Premium is credited separately to Securities Premium Reserve and is not credited to Share Capital Account.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any discount on reissue is charged to the Statement of Profit and Loss.
known_pitfalls.correction: Discount on reissue is debited to Share Forfeiture Account and cannot exceed the amount forfeited on the shares reissued.

recommended_example_progression: Use the Sunrise Company Ltd. example in Section 1.3.1 to classify authorised, issued, subscribed, called-up and paid-up capital.
Use the journal entries and early illustrations in Section 1.6 to record application, allotment and calls.
Use the chapter’s calls-in-arrears and calls-in-advance illustrations to distinguish unpaid calls from money received early.
Use the over-subscription illustrations in Section 1.6.3 for rejection, pro-rata allotment and adjustment of excess application money.
Use the vendor and consideration-other-than-cash illustrations in Section 1.6.7.
Use the forfeiture and reissue illustrations in Sections 1.7 and 1.7.1 to determine Capital Reserve.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions for Practice containing Short Answer, Long Answer and Numerical Questions on categories of capital, issue entries, over-subscription, calls, forfeiture and reissue.
